title: QUIC Connection Migration Hosted Proof Lane Architecture
purpose: Describe the advisory hosted Linux connectionmigration proof lane that refreshes live corroboration for the inventory cell by comparing server-role behavior against neqo with the OCI-indexed neqo-qns image while keeping ngtcp2, lsquic, quiche, quic-go, msquic, and aioquic visible in a blocked comparison lane.
design_summary: The manual hosted workflow keeps the default hosted-handshake and major-peer-matrix profiles unchanged and adds a proof-oriented `connectionmigration-server-proof` profile plus a separate `connectionmigration-server-proof-blocked` profile. The proof profile runs Incursa.Quic as a local server replacement for the distinct `nginx` slot, reports `neqo-peer` as the peer alias, normalizes the actual runner peer slot to `neqo`, and uses the OCI-indexed `neqo` peer image for `connectionmigration`, while the blocked profile preserves `ngtcp2`, `lsquic`, `quiche`, `quic-go`, `msquic`, and `aioquic` comparison cells. Each cell invokes the existing repo-local helper with matrix-supplied role, local implementation slot, peer slot, testcase, timeout, and artifact root. The matrix pre-pulls the selected peer implementation image and uploads each cell bundle with `if: always()` so failed, advisory, blocked, and passing attempts remain attributable. Hosted run `25864019585` cleared the alias lookup failure but exposed a replacement-slot collision (`-s neqo -c neqo -r neqo=incursa-quic-interop-harness:local`), so its later single-path failure is not treated as a real neqo-peer migration verdict. Hosted runs `25866825495` and `25867235353` confirmed the distinct local `nginx` replacement slot and normalized `neqo` runner peer slot, but failed before transfer or migration with server-side `TLS alert 50`. Hosted run `25868496912` kept the correct runner invocation and moved deeper: captured qlog replay opens the server Initial and Handshake first flight with the published secrets and confirms a TLS 1.3 `x25519` ServerHello, while the pcaps show the first server flight sourced from preferred migration address `fd00:cafe:cafe:100::110` instead of the original server address `fd00:cafe:cafe:100::100` that neqo contacted. The harness setup therefore installs the configured preferred migration address with `preferred_lft 0`; this keeps the address reachable for later migration without letting the wildcard listener source the original-path first flight from it. The existing helper/runtime migration support stays the source of truth for the inventory claim; this architecture only explains the hosted evidence-collection lanes that refresh live corroboration without widening the broader major-peer-matrix scope or claiming hosted success before the next proof run passes.
alternatives_considered: Fold connectionmigration into the major peer matrix. Rejected because that matrix is intentionally scoped to currently executable cells and would overstate the broader evidence surface.
Rely on the local migration proof only. Rejected because the gap ledger still requires hosted corroboration and the user explicitly asked to compare against the GitHub-hosted runner.
Change the runtime transport behavior first. Rejected because the runtime seam already exists; the remaining work is hosted proof and evidence collection.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The hosted Linux profiles remain advisory and outside ordinary CI gates.
Every matrix cell must preserve a distinct artifact root so role, peer, and testcase results can be audited independently.
Partial hosted proof, server-only dispatch, or local proof alone must not be treated as support evidence.
The configured preferred migration address must be reachable for connection migration without becoming the kernel-preferred source for the original-path server first flight.
data_and_state_considerations: The proof lane relies on preserved runner artifacts under `artifacts/interop-runner/...` plus the existing gap ledger and current-status notes. The profile writes transient artifacts under `artifacts/interop-runner/<cell>/` and uploads them as GitHub Actions artifacts. No external runner repository changes are required.
risks: Peer-image drift can expose real interop failures or external-runner breakage after local helper planning is green.
The matrix size can increase hosted cost and duration.
Readers may overread the dedicated hosted profile as support promotion unless the advisory boundary stays visible.

supplemental_sections.heading: Scope
supplemental_sections.content: This design only formalizes the dedicated hosted proof lanes for connectionmigration. It does not change HTTP/3, broad rebinding semantics, or the scope of the major-peer-matrix profile.
